messages:
Tara (sales): FYI: NovaHealth POC — blocker from their netsec: they need SNI to reach their DMZ inspector and the original client IP in app logs. Ask: which network topology should we propose (peering vs PrivateLink) and what should go into the SOW for costs and ops?

Omar (solutions): Quick summary: VPC peering preserves client src IP and lets their inline TLS inspector see SNI without extra proxies. PrivateLink isolates access and avoids cross-account routes but endpoint ENIs become the apparent source IP; customer must terminate TLS at their proxy and re-TLS to us or add X-Forwarded-For to surface client IP.

Priya (netops): Two sketches for handoff:
- Peering: Customer-TGW/spoke -> peering -> Redwood-VPC -> app (no NAT, srcIP preserved)
- PrivateLink: Customer-TGW/spoke -> interface endpoint -> endpoint ENI -> Redwood (srcIP = endpoint IP)

Priya (netops): Firewall guidance to give customer ops:
```
# PrivateLink
Allow TCP/443 -> <interface-endpoint-subnet-cidrs>
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-controlplane-ips>  # if control plane needed

# VPC Peering
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-peering-cidr>

# Common
Enforce TLS 1.2+; deny weak ciphers
Log X-Forwarded-For if proxy terminates TLS
```

Ethan (security): For the questionnaire: provide concise KMS/HSM and key custody language: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integration; customer keys are not stored in plaintext. Key usage is audited and exportable. mTLS to customer CAs supported; rotation policy configurable." Also add a note: "If TLS inspection is required in-customer DMZ, the customer must terminate and re-initiate TLS to Redwood."

Tara (sales): They also asked for a ballpark monthly delta for ~5TB. Need a one-line estimate for SOW.

Omar (solutions): Ballpark: PrivateLink infra fees ≈ endpoint hourly (~$0.01/hr) + data processing (~$0.01/GB). For 5TB (~5120GB) that's roughly $50–$70/mo plus cloud egress. Peering: no endpoint/data-processing surcharge; cross-VPC transfer varies (~$0.005–$0.02/GB) → ~$25–$100/mo. Peering typically cheaper at scale but requires peering approvals and route work.

Priya (netops): Ops note: PrivateLink reduces route table changes (faster security sign-off). Peering requires cross-account peering and route table updates (1–2 engineer-hours), but gives native client IP for logs / SIEM correlation.

Tara (sales): Can we offer a hybrid suggestion in SOW if they want both SNI and preserved src IP?

Omar (solutions): Hybrid workable: deploy a small customer-side proxy that terminates TLS (so DMZ inspector sees SNI) then re-TLS to Redwood over peering and set proxy to pass X-Forwarded-For. This keeps srcIP in logs via header plumbing and ensures SNI inspection. Document this as an integration task and list as recommended engineering work in SOW.

handoff-bot: Created ticket RW-4277: "NovaHealth POC - network handoff: SNI & srcIP decision + cost delta" and attached runbook template.

Tara (sales): Thanks — please paste a short SOW paragraph I can drop into the doc.

Omar (solutions): SOW paragraph (copy): "Recommendation: For the NovaHealth POC we recommend VPC peering to Redwood Private when visibility of SNI to an inline TLS inspector and preservation of original client IPs in application logs are required. VPC peering preserves network source IP and allows DMZ inspection without additional TLS proxying. If the customer prohibits cross-account peering, PrivateLink is an alternative that provides stronger isolation but requires TLS termination at the customer proxy (or X-Forwarded-For header insertion) and incurs modest per-GB interface processing fees. The engineering handoff will include firewall allowlists, expected CIDRs, and an onboarding checklist."

Tara (sales): Perfect. I'll send to NovaHealth and mark the ticket for the netops handoff. :white_check_mark:
